data.prompt:
You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: pic-e
Title: Pic rep lane E: close Pic representability, no new hypotheses
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
References: roadmap=AJC.jacobian,AJC.picrep; inbox=I-0838

Pic representability should close, and closing it is your objective — pick a roadmap item and make major progress on it, USING NO ADDITIONAL HYPOTHESIS (`rep` has 93 consumers and 0 producers; last round added 71 more consumers and the headline did not move). Your work must be directly usable by Pic representability and the other items, not local to your row. Be ambitious: don't scope down because something is large or missing from mathlib — building substrate and huge refactoring are licensed. Delete unfaithful roadmap items and create truer ones, but never a row another lane owns at HEAD. Collaborate with the other lanes; announce what you take before you start.

YOUR PEERS this round are pic-a, pic-b, pic-c, pic-d, pic-e, pic-f, pic-g, pic-h — eight provers, no reviewer. Four work Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (pic-a, pic-b, pic-e, pic-f) and four work Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild (pic-c, pic-d, pic-g, pic-h). With eight lanes on one ledger, announcing what you take BEFORE you start is what stops two lanes proving the same lemma — read the inbox for what the others announced, and say so if you are taking something already held.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

data.content:
1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
355

Method note for whoever re-checks any absence claim in this area: a bare
`horizon search picEt` returns ten hits, **all from the sibling project**, because
the result set is capped — reading that as absence in AJC would be a false
negative. Query a specific name (`picEtComparison`) or scan declaration headers
in-tree. Two earlier revisions of this paragraph offered lists called "the
complete list" and **both were wrong** (`I-1075`, and a fresh-context audit that
found six omissions); neither error touched the conclusion, which is why a token
scan rather than a census is what such a claim should rest on.

Item 2 was **not** portable from the sibling project, which was the trap, and the
outcome recorded it: `AJCR` proves a cross-base comparison as a `MulEquiv`
(`picEtCrossBaseEquiv`, `Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean:316`, 468 lines), but its
`picEt` is a hand-built affine-opens limit of plus-classes (`PicEt.lean:105`)
while this file's is a categorical sheafification (`PicEtSheaf.lean:238`) —
different objects, no `lake` edge. Most of that length is a section-ring scalar
tower which a *sheafification*-based `picEt` does not need, because for it the
whole sheafification layer collapses to one Mathlib lemma
(`Functor.pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility`, applicable because
restriction along `Over.map` is continuous for the two localised étale topologies
by pure synthesis). Reading the sibling as a design lead rather than transcribing
it was the cheaper move.

This is the **sole** `sorry` of the seam: everything else below — the
representing scheme `PicSchemeEt`, its representability, local finiteness,
separatedness and group-scheme structure, the comparison theorem
`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and the conditional
`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from it.

**Why the second conjunct is bundled here rather than given its own `sorry`.**
Clause (1) is Kleiman §4; clause (2) is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`): given a
section, the comparison `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is an isomorphism. Both are
theorems of the same paper and neither is formalised. They are stated as one
named obligation on purpose: the `picSharp`-shaped consumer interface
(`HasPicScheme`, and through it the tangent-space chain and the `k̄` Albanese
witness) needs clause (2) to exist at all, and splitting it out would report the
Jacobian headline as resting on *six* open obligations where the mathematics has
five. The bundling adds no strength — clause (2) is conditional on a section, so
it says nothing about a pointless curve — and it keeps the frontier count honest
in both directions. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measures the result rather
than asserting it.

**"Adds no strength" is now MEASURED, and the measurement is sharper than the
claim** (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-30; `lake env lean` EXIT=0 in a scratch file,
since deleted). Both conjuncts of this theorem follow, *together*, from the
single hypothesis

  `∃ X, Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧`
  `      LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom`

— i.e. from the `picSharp`-shaped endpoint that the Milne–Kollár campaign's ten
modules are built to produce, with **nothing left over**. Clause (1) is
`hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` and clause (2) is
`isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` (both
`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`), the second discarding the section it is handed.
Axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The two halves existed
separately; what had not been measured is that their conjunction is exactly this
statement, so no reader had to take "adds no strength" on trust.

**The control here has a trap in it, and the trap is worth more than the
result.** The obvious control — "does the conclusion close *without* the campaign
hypothesis?" — **succeeds**, so read naively it says the reduction is empty.
`exact?` closes clause (1) hypothesis-free via
`HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et`, and clause (2) via
`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`. Both are legitimate terms; both
route through `instHasPicSchemeEt`, which *is* a projection of the `sorry` below.
Measured: the hypothesis-free version reports
`[propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` while the version above
reports no `sorryAx`. So on this seam **provability is not a discriminating
control and the axiom list is** — because an unconditional gate instance makes
every statement in its domain provable. Anyone probing a reduction anywhere near
`HasPicSchemeEt` should compare axiom lists, not success and failure.

**What this does NOT mean, since it is the natural misreading.** It does not
bring the seam closer. The hypothesis is the campaign's *undischarged output*,
and over an arbitrary `k` there is a refutation waiting for it —
`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) turns any failure of
`IsIso (picEtComparison C)` into a refutation of the existential, and Kleiman's
pointless real conic is where that failure is expected.

**Stated precisely, because the first version of this paragraph overstated it**
(`review-ajc`, corrected within the same session): that refutation is
*conditional* on `¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)`, which is **quoted from Kleiman,
not proved in this project** — `PicEtSubcanonical.lean` says so itself, and
formalising it means exhibiting `φ*O(1)` in `picEt C (Spec ℝ)` outside the image
via `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`. So the honest word for the campaign's `picSharp` endpoint
over arbitrary `k` is **unproved with a refutation route mapped out**, not
"FALSE" — the reduction above is a theorem, its trigger is not. Writing "FALSE"
here would be the same error the board row was corrected for in the opposite
direction.

Either way the consequence for planning is unchanged: whatever the campaign
delivers must be delivered over a field where `picSharp` is representable (a
separably closed one, or under a section), and the descent to `k` must carry
`picEt` points — and if it does deliver that, this bundled statement is fully
discharged, with clause (2) costing zero extra work. -/
theorem fgaPicardRepresentability {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    (∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom)
      ∧ (HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
  sorry

/-- **The étale representability gate**, as a `Prop`-class so that consumers can
quantify over it as a hypothesis.

Unlike the legacy `HasPicScheme`, this class carries **no** hypothesis on
`C(k)`: its unique producer `instHasPicSchemeEt` is unconditional. It is the
carrier of the project's central open obligation.

**It is not a gate, and quantifying over it does not keep a consumer
kernel-clean** — the previous sentence here promised that and it is
undeliverable (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-29). Because `instHasPicSchemeEt` is
unconditional, instance search discharges this class for every object in its own
domain, so a consumer that binds it is `sorryAx`-reachable the moment it is
applied; there is no `C` in the domain for which the binder is a real
restriction. Contrast `HasPicScheme`, which has no instance at all and for which
the binder genuinely is a hypothesis. What this class does buy is the shape:
statements quantified over it read as implications and are stated for an
arbitrary base field, per `I-0491`. See `PicSchemeEt` below for the
measurement. -/
class HasPicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where
  has_pic_scheme_et : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
    Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom

/-- The étale gate fires for **every** smooth proper geometrically integral
curve, with no rational-point hypothesis — which is the whole content of the
owner decision of 2026-07-28. Its mathematics is
`fgaPicardRepresentability`, the one open obligation. -/
instance instHasPicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : HasPicSchemeEt C :=
  ⟨(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1⟩

152	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`) is
153	stated *about an action*, so a consumer cannot discharge it before knowing which
154	action it will face. This form is a property of the scheme alone, and §2 shows it
155	implies the action form for **every** semilinear action of a finite Galois group.
156	That is what lets the antecedent of §4 be stated without mentioning the Galois
157	level, which is chosen inside the proof.
158	
159	True for quasi-projective schemes (finite point sets of a quasi-projective scheme
160	lie in an affine open). Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity vocabulary at
161	this pin, which is why the hypothesis is carried in this elementary form rather
162	than derived. -/
163	def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
164	  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
165	
166	/-- **The pointed Picard theorem**: FGA/Kleiman representability of the relative
167	Picard functor, for curves that *have* a rational point, uniformly in the base
168	field, together with quasi-projectivity of the representing scheme.
169	
170	This is the campaign's target, written as a closed proposition. Three things about
171	its shape are deliberate, and a fourth is deliberately **absent**.
172	
173	* It quantifies over **all** base fields `K`, not just over `k`. That is
174	  essential and it is not a strengthening in any useful sense: §4 applies it at a
175	  finite Galois extension of `k` chosen by the curve, so a version fixed at `k`
176	  would not compose. Every formalisation route to FGA representability is uniform
177	  in the base field anyway.
178	* It is about `picSharp`, the **unsheafified** relative Picard functor — the object
179	  the Milne–Kollár modules target (`I-0907`). No étale-sheafified representability
180	  statement is needed on top of it; §3 of `Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` supplies
181	  the transport for free.
182	* `FiniteInAffine X.left` is bundled rather than carried separately so that the
183	  results below have **one** antecedent. The *property* is perfectly stateable
184	  outside it — `HasGoodGaloisLevel` in §5 does exactly that, and §2 takes it as a
185	  free-standing hypothesis. What cannot be stated outside is the **witness**: no
186	  separate binder can name the scheme the antecedent itself produces. (An earlier
187	  revision of this bullet said the property "cannot be stated outside it", which
188	  two declarations in this same file refute.)
189	* **`IsSeparated X.hom` is NOT a conjunct**, and carrying it would have
190	  misreported the price of the reduction. It is *free* from the resulting `picEt`
191	  representation by `isSeparated_of_representableBy_picEt`
192	  (`Picard/PicEtSeparated.lean`) — Yoneda transports the `CommGrpCat`-valued
193	  functor's group structure onto any representing scheme, and a group scheme over
194	  a field is separated. That file's
195	  `picEtClauseOne_of_picSharp_representableBy_locallyOfFiniteType` already says
196	  in its own docstring that the form to hand the campaign asks "nothing about
197	  separatedness". A first revision of this file bundled it anyway; a
198	  fresh-context audit reproved every result with the conjunct deleted, so it is
199	  deleted. The seam's clause (1) still *concludes* separatedness — it is
200	  discharged, not dropped. -/
201	def PointedPicSharpRep : Prop :=
202	  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
203	    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
204	      Scheme.HasRationalPoint E →
205	      ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
206	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy X) ∧
207	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ FiniteInAffine X.left
208	
209	/-! ## §2. The scheme-level hypothesis implies the action-level one -/
210	
211	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` discharges `OrbitsInAffineOpen`, for every semilinear
212	action of a finite Galois group.**
213	
214	The orbit of a point is the range of a map indexed by `L ≃ₐ[K] L`, which is finite
215	because `L/K` is finite Galois (`Finite (L ≃ₐ[K] L)` by synthesis), so it is a
216	finite subset and the hypothesis applies directly.
217	
218	Note where the finiteness of the group is consumed: only here. The quotient
219	machinery downstream binds `[FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]` for its own
220	reasons. -/
221	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
222	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
223	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
224	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
225	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
226	    ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
227	  exists_affineOpen x := by
228	    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
229	      h (Set.range fun γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (ρ.act γ).hom.base x) (Set.finite_range _)
230	    exact ⟨U, fun γ => hU ⟨γ, rfl⟩⟩
231	
232	/-! ## §3. `FiniteInAffine` is inhabited, and is not free
233	
234	Both directions are recorded as declarations rather than as docstring sentences,
235	per `I-0838`: a hypothesis whose satisfiability is unmeasured is how a vacuous
236	statement survives, and a hypothesis that is *free* would make the results below
237	empty. -/
238	
239	/-- **Non-vacuity**: an affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`, with `⊤` as the
240	affine open. So the antecedent of §4 is not asserting something about no scheme.
241	
242	This is the cheap witness, and it is the honest one to give: it is *not* a witness
243	at a Picard scheme, and no such witness exists in this project. What it rules out
244	is the failure mode where `FiniteInAffine` is unsatisfiable and the results below
245	are vacuously true. -/
246	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] : FiniteInAffine X :=
247	  fun _ _ => ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ => trivial⟩
248	
249	/-! ## §4. The reduction
250	
251	Clause (2) first, because it needs strictly less. -/
252	
253	/-- **Clause (2) of the seam, from the pointed antecedent alone.**
254	
255	No Galois level, no quotient, no orbit hypothesis, and the `FiniteInAffine`
256	conjunct of the antecedent is discarded: given a section, the antecedent applies
257	to `C` *itself*, and subcanonicity of the étale topology turns a representation
258	into invertibility of the comparison map
259	(`isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability`).
260	
261	So of the seam's two conjuncts, this one costs nothing beyond the pointed theorem.
262	That is a sharper statement than the seam docstring's "clause (2) costs zero extra
263	work", which was said relative to a `picSharp`-shaped endpoint over the *same*
264	field; here it is said relative to the pointed antecedent, which is the thing
265	actually being assumed. -/
266	theorem seamClauseTwo_of_pointedPicSharpRep {k : Type u} [Field k]
267	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
268	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
269	    (H : PointedPicSharpRep.{u}) :
270	    Scheme.HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C) := by
271	  intro hpt
272	  obtain ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, -, -⟩ := H C hpt
273	  exact isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability C rep
274	
275	/-- **Clause (1) of the seam, over an ARBITRARY field, from the pointed
276	antecedent.** This is the theorem the file exists for.
277	
278	The proof is the composition the module docstring describes, and each step is a
279	landed sorry-free theorem of a different lane:
280	
281	1. `exists_finiteGalois_level_hasRationalPoint_of_geometricallyIntegral` produces
282	   a finite **Galois** `k''/k` and a rational point on `C_{k''}` — unconditionally,
283	   from `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1]` and `[GeometricallyIntegral]` alone. This
284	   is the only step that uses `GeometricallyIntegral`.
285	2. The antecedent, applied at `k''` to the base-changed curve (all three binders
286	   are stable under field base change, by synthesis), gives a scheme representing
287	   `picSharp (C_{k''})` with the two side conjuncts and `FiniteInAffine`.
288	3. `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` converts it to a `picEt`
289	   representation — the same scheme, so `LocallyOfFiniteType` rides along.
290	4. §2 turns `FiniteInAffine` into `OrbitsInAffineOpen` at the canonical semilinear
291	   action `semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep`, which is the action the
292	   descent step uses.
293	5. `seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree` descends to `k`, discharging the
294	   quotient and the covering sieve internally.
295	
296	The conclusion is over `k` with **no** section and **no** `k''` in sight, and no
297	hypothesis of the theorem mentions a representation of `picEt C` — so this is not
298	`P → P`, and it is not the refuted shape of `representableByRestrict_of_baseChange`
299	(`I-1312`), which concluded about a `k'`-object. -/
300	theorem seamClauseOne_of_pointedPicSharpRep {k : Type u} [Field k]
301	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
302	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
303	    (H : PointedPicSharpRep.{u}) :
304	    ∃ Z : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
305	      Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy Z) ∧
306	        LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom ∧ IsSeparated Z.hom := by
307	  obtain ⟨k'', hfd, hgal, hpt⟩ :=
308	    Scheme.exists_finiteGalois_level_hasRationalPoint_of_geometricallyIntegral C
309	  letI := hfd
310	  letI := hgal
311	  obtain ⟨X', ⟨rep0⟩, hft, hfa⟩ := H (Scheme.baseChangeField C (k'' : Type u)) hpt
312	  letI rep :=
313	    picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport (Scheme.baseChangeField C (k'' : Type u)) rep0
314	  letI := orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
315	    (PicScheme.semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) hfa
316	  exact PicScheme.seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree rep hft
317	
318	/-- **The seam, verbatim, as the conclusion of an implication.**
319	
320	The conclusion is character-for-character the statement of
321	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`, so a lane that proves `PointedPicSharpRep`
322	closes the project's central `sorry` by `exact`. Stated as a named theorem rather
323	than left to the reader to assemble, because "the two clauses are available
324	separately" is not the same as "the seam follows", and the difference is exactly
325	the kind of joint that goes unchecked. -/
326	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep {k : Type u} [Field k]
327	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
328	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
329	    (H : PointedPicSharpRep.{u}) :
330	    (∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
331	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
332	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom)
333	      ∧ (Scheme.HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
334	  ⟨seamClauseOne_of_pointedPicSharpRep C H, seamClauseTwo_of_pointedPicSharpRep C H⟩
335	
336	/-! ## §5. The weakest antecedent clause (1) actually needs
337	
338	§4 states the reduction against `PointedPicSharpRep`, which is the shape a
339	*campaign* delivers: uniform in the field, stated with a rational-point
340	hypothesis. That is the right form for a hand-off, and it is deliberately
341	stronger than the proof consumes. This section writes down what clause (1) really
342	needs, because a reduction priced against an over-strong antecedent misreports
343	what is left.
344	
345	Three things fall away, and each is a fact about the proof rather than a
346	restatement.
347	
348	* **The uniformity in the field.** Only ONE extension is used. Not "all
349	  fields", not even "all finite Galois levels of `k`" — a single good level
350	  suffices, so the antecedent is an existential.
351	* **The rational point.** It does not occur in `HasGoodGaloisLevel` at all. In §4
352	  it is the *route* by which the level is produced (via
353	  `exists_finiteGalois_level_hasRationalPoint_of_geometricallyIntegral`), but the
354	  descent step never looks at it. A lane that can represent `picSharp` over some
355	  finite Galois extension by any other means owes no section.
356	* **`[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]` and `IsSeparated`.** The former is used in §4
357	  *only* to produce the level, so with the level assumed it is not a binder here
358	  — this theorem holds for a smooth proper `C` with no integrality hypothesis at
359	  all. The latter is not an input in either form: it comes from the group
360	  structure of the represented object (`PicEtSeparated`, consumed inside
361	  `seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree`).
362	
363	**On the converse — and this paragraph is a CORRECTION of what stood here.** The
364	first revision said the converse "fails even at the trivial extension `k' = k`",
365	evidenced by `exact?` failing on
366	`Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy Z)` from `(picEt C).RepresentableBy Z`,
367	and gave as the reason that the `PicEtSubcanonical.lean` transport "runs
368	`picSharp → picEt` only, because it is the sheafification unit". **The reason was
369	false and the probe was inadequate** (fresh-context audit, reproduced here before
370	accepting). The comparison is a *morphism*; once it is an iso,
371	`RepresentableBy.ofIso` runs both ways, and
372	
373	  `converseOfIsIso : IsIso (picEtComparison C) → (picEt C).RepresentableBy Z →`
374	  `  Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy Z)`
375	
376	is the three-line term below — the same term already landed inside
377	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), i.e. in this
378	file's own import closure, which the withdrawn paragraph did not mention. And the
379	hypothesis it needs is supplied by **clause (2) of this file's own antecedent**:
380	under `PointedPicSharpRep`, `seamClauseTwo_of_pointedPicSharpRep` gives
381	`IsIso (picEtComparison C)` at every curve *with a section*.
382	
383	So the honest statement is narrower than "not equivalent" and sharper than
384	"equivalent": the two representability notions are **interderivable at every
385	pointed curve**, and the gap is confined exactly to curves with **no** rational
386	point — where `¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)` is Kleiman's pointless real conic,
387	quoted in `Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` and *not proved* in this project. That
388	is still a genuine gap and this is still not a change of coordinates, but the
389	reason is the pointless case, not the direction of the unit. Contrast
390	`coverCompatibleEquiv_of_representableBy`
391	(`Picard/PicEtDescentRepresentability.lean`), whose converse is unconditional. -/
392	def HasGoodGaloisLevel {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
393	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] : Prop :=
394	  ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k'),
395	    ∃ (_ : FiniteDimensional k k') (_ : IsGalois k k')
396	      (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))),
397	      Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).RepresentableBy X) ∧
398	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ FiniteInAffine X.left
399

781	  /-- The quotient map `O_{X_T} ⟶ O_D` (source stated as the pulled-back
782	  unit, as in `QuotFamily` with `E = O_X`). -/
783	  q : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj
784	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ⟶ F
785	  /-- The quotient map is an epimorphism. -/
786	  epi : Epi q
787	  /-- **The divisor condition** (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:red`): the kernel ideal
788	  `I = ker q` is invertible, i.e. locally trivial of rank one. -/
789	  kerLocallyTrivial : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (Limits.kernel q)
790	
791	namespace DivFamily
792	
793	variable {π : X ⟶ S}
794	
795	/-- Two families of divisors are **equivalent** when an isomorphism of the
796	target sheaves commutes with the quotient maps — equivalently, when
797	`ker q = ker q'` as subobjects of `O_{X_T}`, i.e. when they cut out the same
798	closed subscheme (same convention as `QuotFamily.Rel`). -/
799	def Rel {T : Over S} (x y : DivFamily π T) : Prop :=
800	  ∃ f : x.F ≅ y.F, x.q ≫ f.hom = y.q
801	
802	lemma rel_refl {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T) : x.Rel x :=
803	  ⟨Iso.refl _, Category.comp_id _⟩
804	
805	lemma rel_symm {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) : y.Rel x := by
806	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
807	  exact ⟨f.symm, by rw [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq]; exact hf.symm⟩
808	
809	lemma rel_trans {T : Over S} {x y z : DivFamily π T}
810	    (h1 : x.Rel y) (h2 : y.Rel z) : x.Rel z := by
811	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h1; obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := h2
812	  exact ⟨f ≪≫ g,
813	    (congrArg (x.q ≫ ·) (Iso.trans_hom f g)).trans <|
814	      (Category.assoc x.q f.hom g.hom).symm.trans <|
815	        (congrArg (· ≫ g.hom) hf).trans hg⟩
816	
817	/-- The equivalence-of-families setoid. -/
818	instance setoid (π : X ⟶ S) (T : Over S) : Setoid (DivFamily π T) where
819	  r := Rel
820	  iseqv := ⟨rel_refl, rel_symm, rel_trans⟩
821	
822	/-- The **pullback action** on a family of divisors along `ψ : T' ⟶ T` of
823	`Over S`: pull the sheaf and the quotient map back along
824	`quotBaseMap π ψ : X_{T'} ⟶ X_T`, matching the `O`-side through
825	`pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)` — exactly
826	`QuotFamily.pullbackAlong` at `E = O_X`.  The divisor condition base-changes
827	by `Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial`
828	(`lem:relative_divisor_base_change`). -/
829	noncomputable def pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T)
830	    (x : DivFamily π T) : DivFamily π T' where
831	  F := (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).obj x.F
832	  isFinitePresentation :=
833	    Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation _ x.F x.isFinitePresentation
834	  flat := fun {_} hU {_} hV e =>
835	    CoherentSheafFlat.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
836	      (letI := x.isFinitePresentation; inferInstance) x.flat hU hV e
837	  properSupport :=
838	    Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.F
839	      x.isFinitePresentation x.properSupport
840	  q := (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
841	      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv ≫
842	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q
843	  epi :=
844	    @CategoryTheory.epi_comp _ _ _ _ _
845	      (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
846	        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv inferInstance
847	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)
848	      (@CategoryTheory.Functor.map_epi _ _ _ _
849	        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)) inferInstance _ _ x.q x.epi)
850	  kerLocallyTrivial :=
851	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
852	      (kernelIsIsoComp
853	        (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst π ψ)
854	          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).inv
855	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ)).map x.q)).symm
856	      (Modules.pullback_kernel_isLocallyTrivial (quotBaseSquare π ψ) x.q x.epi
857	        (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst π T.hom)
858	          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
859	        x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial)
860	
861	/-- The pullback action respects the equivalence relation. -/
862	lemma pullbackAlong_rel {T T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T)
863	    {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) :
864	    (pullbackAlong ψ x).Rel (pullbackAlong ψ y) := by

/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is smooth over `k`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, and a **true**
statement.

Kleiman §5: a group scheme locally of finite type over a field is smooth as soon
as it is geometrically reduced. Mathlib's `smooth_of_grpObj` takes exactly
`[LocallyOfFiniteType f]`, `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` and `[GeometricallyReduced f]`
over an arbitrary field, and the first two are proved above
(`locallyOfFiniteType`, `grpObj`). So the entire remaining content is
`GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom` — Cartier's theorem in
characteristic zero, and a genuine characteristic-`p` statement otherwise. It
does not synthesize, and its only producer in the tree is
`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular.

This is the étale-formulation counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.smooth`, and it is one
of the five obligations of the Jacobian headline. Following the run-0067 reduction
of the `picSharp` side (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`), it is stated here as an
**assembly** rather than an obligation: the translation argument is mathlib's and
the two other inputs are proved above, so the obligation proper is
`geometricallyReduced` below and nothing else. -/
theorem smooth_of_geometricallyReduced {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C]
    (h : GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
    Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
  haveI := h
  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) := (grpObj C).some
  exact smooth_of_grpObj (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom

/-- **The sole remaining input to smoothness: geometric reducedness of
`Pic⁰_{C/k}`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, a **true** statement.

Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero; in characteristic `p` a genuine
statement (it is where `H²(C, 𝒪_C) = 0` enters on the `picSharp` side). It does
not synthesize, and its only producer in the tree is
`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular here.

This is the étale counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyReduced`. -/
theorem geometricallyReduced {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
  sorry

/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is smooth over `k`** — assembly of
`smooth_of_geometricallyReduced` with its single open input. -/
theorem smooth {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
  smooth_of_geometricallyReduced C (geometricallyReduced C)

/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is proper over `k`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, and a **true**
statement.

Kleiman §5 Prp. `prp:pic0`: the identity component of the Picard scheme of a
smooth proper curve is proper (indeed projective) over the base. Quasi-compactness
of the identity component is available
(`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`, second
conjunct) and separatedness descends from `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated` along the
clopen immersion; what is missing is universal closedness, which is where the
properness of `C` enters through the Abel map.

This is the étale-formulation counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.proper`, and it is one
of the five obligations of the Jacobian headline. As with smoothness, it is stated
as an **assembly**: two of the three conjuncts of properness are proved, so the
obligation proper is `universallyClosed` below. -/
theorem isSeparated {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
  obtain ⟨⟨f, hopen, -⟩⟩ :=
    GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme (PicSchemeEt C)
  haveI := hopen
  change IsSeparated (GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicSchemeEt C)).hom
  rw [← Over.w f]
  infer_instance

/-- **The sole remaining input to properness: universal closedness of
`Pic⁰_{C/k}`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, a **true** statement.

Kleiman §5 Thm. `th:qpp&p`: a smooth proper curve is geometrically normal, so the
projectivity upgrade applies to its Picard scheme and the identity component is
proper. Separatedness (`isSeparated` above, from `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`
along the clopen immersion) and local finiteness (`locallyOfFiniteType`) are the
two conjuncts that are proved; this is the third.

This is the étale counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.universallyClosed`. -/
theorem universallyClosed {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    UniversallyClosed (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
  sorry

/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is proper over `k`** — assembly of the two proved conjuncts
with the single open one. -/
theorem proper {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    IsProper (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
  haveI : IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := isSeparated C
  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
  haveI := universallyClosed C
  constructor

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- **Transport of the fibre-section dimension along an isomorphism of fibre
modules.**  An isomorphism of sheaves of modules on the scheme-theoretic fibre
`π₀.fiber s` induces a `κ(s)`-linear equivalence on global sections
(evaluation at `⊤` is functorial, and the `κ(s)`-scalar action factors through
`Scheme.Hom.fiberResidueMap`), so the `κ(s)`-dimensions agree.  Twist-free
sibling of `Scheme.hilbertFunction_eq_finrank_of_iso`
(`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), serving the degree lane where no tensor
operations may enter. -/
lemma finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso {W B : Scheme.{u}} (π₀ : W ⟶ B) (s : B)
    {G G' : (π₀.fiber s).Modules} (e : G ≅ G') :
    (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
     Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G, ⊤))
      = (letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
         Module.finrank (B.residueField s) Γ(G', ⊤)) := by
  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G
  letI := π₀.fiberSectionsModule s G'
  have γe := ((Scheme.Modules.toPresheafOfModules (π₀.fiber s) ⋙
    PresheafOfModules.evaluation (π₀.fiber s).ringCatSheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)).mapIso
      e).toLinearEquiv
  exact LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
    { toFun := γe
      map_add' := γe.map_add
      map_smul' := fun c x => γe.map_smul ((π₀.fiberResidueMap s).hom c) x
      invFun := γe.symm
      left_inv := γe.left_inv
      right_inv := γe.right_inv }

/-! ## §1. The fibre degree of a family of relative effective divisors -/

namespace DivFamily

variable {π : X ⟶ S}

/-- The **fibre degree** of a family of relative effective divisors
`x : DivFamily π T` at a point `t : T` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`):

  `deg D_t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,

the `κ(t)`-dimension of the global sections of the restriction of the divisor
structure sheaf `F = O_D` to the scheme-theoretic fibre `(X_T)_t`.  This is
the pointwise shadow of "rank of the finite-flat pushforward `q_* O_D`" (equal
to it whenever the pushforward exists as a locally free module, i.e. in the
relative-curve regime once the B3 engine lands; see the module docstring
audit).  `Module.finrank` junk value `0` in the infinite-dimensional case. -/
noncomputable def fiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T)
    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : ℕ :=
  letI := (pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
    ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F)
  Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)
    Γ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t x.F, ⊤)

/-- **The fibre degree is well defined on divisor classes**: equivalent
families (`DivFamily.Rel`, i.e. same divisor `ker q = ker q'`) have equal
fibre degrees — the target isomorphism restricts to each fibre and transports
the section dimension. -/
theorem Rel.fiberDeg_eq {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
    (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) : x.fiberDeg t = y.fiberDeg t := by
  obtain ⟨f, -⟩ := h
  exact finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso (pullback.snd π T.hom) t
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).mapIso f)

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
-- Heartbeat headroom: instantiating the Γ-fibre base-change core provisions
-- pullback/pushforward and field instances under binders, as in the sibling
-- engines of `QuotFunctorDef`.
/-- **The fibre degree is stable under base change** (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`;
Kleiman §3, functoriality of `Div`): for `ψ : T' ⟶ T` and `t' : T'` over
`t := ψ(t')`, the fibre degree of the pulled-back family at `t'` equals the
fibre degree of `x` at `t`.

Route (all inputs axiom-clean): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is the base
change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t` along `Spec κ(t') → Spec κ(t)`
(`Scheme.isPullback_fiberBaseChange`, the `quotBaseSquare`/residue-field
pasting); the two fibre restrictions of `F` are matched by pseudofunctor
coherence (`Scheme.pullbackSquareIso`); proper support of `F/T` restricts to
the fibre (`Modules.HasProperSupport.of_isPullback` on Mathlib's fibre
square); and the twist-free Γ-fibre flat base-change core
`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean` — support descent `G ≅ i_* i^* G` + the
         Module.finrank (T.left.residueField t)
          Γ(Limits.cokernel
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberι t)).map
                (Limits.kernel.ι x.q)), ⊤)) :=
  (finrank_fiberSections_eq_of_iso (pullback.snd π T.hom) t
    (x.fiberCokernelIso t)).symm

/-! ## §3. Constant-degree families -/

/-- A divisor family **has (constant) fibre degree `d`** when every fibre
divisor has degree `d` (Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`).  Vacuously true for every
`d` when `T` is empty — which is why the degree pieces of `DivFunctor` are
pairwise disjoint only over nonempty bases (`ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`). -/
def HasFiberDeg {T : Over S} (x : DivFamily π T) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : (T.left : Scheme.{u}), x.fiberDeg t = d

/-- Constant fibre degree is invariant under the divisor equivalence
(`DivFamily.Rel`): well-definedness input for the degree slice of the
quotient functor. -/
theorem Rel.hasFiberDeg_iff {T : Over S} {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y)
    (d : ℕ) : x.HasFiberDeg d ↔ y.HasFiberDeg d :=
  forall_congr' fun t => by rw [h.fiberDeg_eq t]

/-- Constant fibre degree is stable under arbitrary base change — the degree
slice `DivFunctorDeg` is a subfunctor, not just a sub-presheaf-of-sets.
Immediate from `fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`. -/
theorem HasFiberDeg.pullbackAlong {T T' : Over S} {x : DivFamily π T} {d : ℕ}
    (hx : x.HasFiberDeg d) (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
    (x.pullbackAlong ψ).HasFiberDeg d :=
  fun t' => (fiberDeg_pullbackAlong ψ x t').trans (hx (ψ.left.base t'))

arbitrary-field difficulty that `I-0491` deliberately put on the headline is now
**discharged**, and what is left is the classical pointed theorem plus
quasi-projectivity of the representing scheme.

And it is an equivalence **at pointed curves** — §6 proves the converse there, so
away from the pointless case this is a change of coordinates and not a discount.
§5 locates the residual gap: curves with no rational point, where
`¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)` is quoted from Kleiman and unproved here.

Finally, per §7, `PointedPicSharpRep` is *derivable from the seam itself* up to
`FiniteInAffine`. So a claimed proof of it must be **axiom-checked**: on this seam
provability is not a discriminating control and the axiom list is.

`FiniteInAffine` is not free: `exact?` fails on it at an arbitrary scheme
(measured, control in the same probe as the results). It is also not vacuous — §3
inhabits it at an affine scheme.
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry
open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

universe u

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/-! ## §1. The two hypotheses, named -/

/-- **Every finite subset lies in a single affine open** — the action-free,
scheme-level form of the EGA II 4.5.4 orbit hypothesis.

`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`) is
stated *about an action*, so a consumer cannot discharge it before knowing which
action it will face. This form is a property of the scheme alone, and §2 shows it
implies the action form for **every** semilinear action of a finite Galois group.
That is what lets the antecedent of §4 be stated without mentioning the Galois
level, which is chosen inside the proof.

True for quasi-projective schemes (finite point sets of a quasi-projective scheme
lie in an affine open). Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity vocabulary at
this pin, which is why the hypothesis is carried in this elementary form rather
than derived. -/
def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1

/-- **The pointed Picard theorem**: FGA/Kleiman representability of the relative
Picard functor, for curves that *have* a rational point, uniformly in the base
field, together with quasi-projectivity of the representing scheme.

This is the campaign's target, written as a closed proposition. Three things about
its shape are deliberate, and a fourth is deliberately **absent**.

* It quantifies over **all** base fields `K`, not just over `k`. That is
  essential and it is not a strengthening in any useful sense: §4 applies it at a
  finite Galois extension of `k` chosen by the curve, so a version fixed at `k`
  would not compose. Every formalisation route to FGA representability is uniform
  in the base field anyway.
* It is about `picSharp`, the **unsheafified** relative Picard functor — the object
  the Milne–Kollár modules target (`I-0907`). No étale-sheafified representability
  statement is needed on top of it; §3 of `Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` supplies
  the transport for free.
* `FiniteInAffine X.left` is bundled rather than carried separately so that the
  results below have **one** antecedent. The *property* is perfectly stateable
  outside it — `HasGoodGaloisLevel` in §5 does exactly that, and §2 takes it as a
  free-standing hypothesis. What cannot be stated outside is the **witness**: no
  separate binder can name the scheme the antecedent itself produces. (An earlier
  revision of this bullet said the property "cannot be stated outside it", which
  two declarations in this same file refute.)
* **`IsSeparated X.hom` is NOT a conjunct**, and carrying it would have
  misreported the price of the reduction. It is *free* from the resulting `picEt`
  representation by `isSeparated_of_representableBy_picEt`
  (`Picard/PicEtSeparated.lean`) — Yoneda transports the `CommGrpCat`-valued
  functor's group structure onto any representing scheme, and a group scheme over
  a field is separated. That file's
  `picEtClauseOne_of_picSharp_representableBy_locallyOfFiniteType` already says
  in its own docstring that the form to hand the campaign asks "nothing about
  separatedness". A first revision of this file bundled it anyway; a
  fresh-context audit reproved every result with the conjunct deleted, so it is
  deleted. The seam's clause (1) still *concludes* separatedness — it is
  discharged, not dropped. -/
def PointedPicSharpRep : Prop :=
  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
      Scheme.HasRationalPoint E →
      ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy X) ∧
          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ FiniteInAffine X.left

/-! ## §2. The scheme-level hypothesis implies the action-level one -/

/-- **`FiniteInAffine` discharges `OrbitsInAffineOpen`, for every semilinear
action of a finite Galois group.**

The orbit of a point is the range of a map indexed by `L ≃ₐ[K] L`, which is finite
because `L/K` is finite Galois (`Finite (L ≃ₐ[K] L)` by synthesis), so it is a
finite subset and the hypothesis applies directly.

Note where the finiteness of the group is consumed: only here. The quotient
machinery downstream binds `[FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]` for its own
reasons. -/
theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
    ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
  exists_affineOpen x := by
    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
      h (Set.range fun γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (ρ.act γ).hom.base x) (Set.finite_range _)
    exact ⟨U, fun γ => hU ⟨γ, rfl⟩⟩

    16	data, hence a closed immersion into a relative projective space.  The existing
    17	nonconstant-map construction produces that finite morphism under exactly the
    18	ambient hypotheses of the algebraic Jacobian challenge.

    42	/-- A smooth proper geometrically integral relative curve is projective over

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Projective morphisms
    10	
    11	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    12	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    13	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    14	
    15	The line-bundle-carrying refinement used by the Quot construction remains in
    16	`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean`; that refinement is universe-monomorphic because
    17	its Serre twist is built by the project-local sheaf gluing engine.
    18	-/

    20	open CategoryTheory Limits
    21	
    22	noncomputable section
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    29	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    30	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    31	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    32	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    33	
    34	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    35	
    36	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    37	
    38	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    39	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    40	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    41	  letI : Finite n := hn
    42	  haveI := hi
    43	  rw [← hcomp]
    44	  infer_instance
    45	
    46	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    47	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    48	  haveI := h.isProper
    49	  inferInstance
    50	
    51	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    52	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    53	  haveI := h.isProper
    54	  inferInstance
    55	
    56	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    57	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    58	  haveI := h.isProper
    59	  inferInstance
    60	
    61	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    62	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    63	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    64	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    65	  letI : Finite n := hn
    66	  haveI := hi
    67	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    70	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    71	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    72	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    73	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    74	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    75	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    76	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
    77	
    78	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
    79	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    80	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
    81	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    82	  letI : Finite n := hn
    83	  haveI := hi
    84	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
    85	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
    86	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    87	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
    88	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
    89	      have hbig : IsPullback
    90	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
    91	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
    92	        rw [h1, hcomp]
    93	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
    94	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
    95	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
    96	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
    97	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
    98	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    99

    54	
    55	/-- The Serre twist `O(m)` on the relative projective space `ℙ(n₀; S)`:
    56	the pullback of the glued twisting sheaf on the integral model. -/
    57	def twistingSheaf (m : ℕ) : (ℙ(n₀; S)).Modules :=
    58	  (Scheme.Modules.pullback (toProjInt n₀ S)).obj (ProjTwist.serreTwist n₀ m)
    59	
    60	variable {S} {S' : Scheme.{0}}
    61	
    62	/-- The Serre twist commutes with base change of the ambient projective
    63	space: `(map g)^* O(m) ≅ O(m)`. -/
    64	def twistingSheafBaseChange (g : S' ⟶ S) (m : ℕ) :
    65	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (map n₀ g)).obj (twistingSheaf n₀ S m) ≅
    66	      twistingSheaf n₀ S' m :=
    67	  Scheme.pullbackTriangleIso (map_toProjInt n₀ g) (ProjTwist.serreTwist n₀ m)
    68	
    69	end ProjectiveSpace
    70	
    71	/-- `π : X ⟶ S` is a **projective morphism carrying the line bundle `L`**
    72	([Nitsure] §5, [EGA II] 5.5): there are a finite coordinate type `n`, a closed
    73	immersion `i : X ↪ ℙ(n; S)` over `S`, and an isomorphism of `L` with the
    74	pullback of the Serre twist `O(1)`.  This is the faithful encoding of
    75	"projective with relatively very ample `L`" settled in inbox `I-0118`. -/
    76	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith {X S : Scheme.{0}} (π : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules) :
    77	    Prop :=
    78	  ∃ (n : Type) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    79	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = π ∧
    80	      Nonempty (L ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj
    81	        (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1))
    82	
    83	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    84	
    85	variable {X S : Scheme.{0}} {π : X ⟶ S}
    86	
    87	/-- Every projective morphism carries a relatively very ample line bundle: choose the
    88	pullback of `O(1)` along the closed immersion in the `IsProjective` witness. -/
    89	theorem exists_isProjectiveWith (h : π.IsProjective) :
    90	    ∃ L : X.Modules, π.IsProjectiveWith L := by
    91	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    92	  letI : Finite n := hn
    93	  let L := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj
    94	    (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1)
    95	  exact ⟨L, n, inferInstance, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨Iso.refl _⟩⟩
    96	
    97	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    98	
    99	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith
   100	
   101	variable {X S : Scheme.{0}} {π : X ⟶ S} {L : X.Modules}
   102	
   103	/-- Forget the chosen very ample line bundle from a projective morphism. -/
   104	theorem isProjective (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : π.IsProjective := by
   105	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, -⟩ := h
   106	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩
   107	
   108	/-- **Projective morphisms are proper**: a closed immersion is proper, the
   109	structural morphism of projective space is proper, and properness is stable
   110	under composition. -/
   111	theorem isProper (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : IsProper π := by
   112	  exact h.isProjective.isProper

   115	`isProper`, since properness extends `LocallyOfFiniteType`.  This lets the

   118	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : LocallyOfFiniteType π :=
   119	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance

   122	theorem isSeparated (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : IsSeparated π :=
   123	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance

   126	`UniversallyClosed`). -/

   128	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance
